item.title: Genkai Seaside Park — Guide
item.description: Genkai Seaside Park, on the scenic northern coast of Saga facing the Genkai Sea, is a spacious coastal park that makes a relaxed family destination. Its wide lawns, gardens and open spaces are planted with seasonal flowers that add colour through the year, and paths lead to viewpoints and walks along the shore with views over the sea and coastline. The park typically has play areas and open grass for children, picnic spots, and space to relax with the sea breeze, making it popular with local families.

item.title: Tottori Seashore Park: Green Space by the Sea — Guide
item.description: Tottori’s seashore park is a broad, well-kept coastal green space near the sand dunes, offering a gentle counterpoint to the stark desert landscape just along the coast. Wide lawns, seasonal flower beds, tree-lined paths and open views over the Sea of Japan make it a relaxed spot for a walk, a picnic or letting children run around, popular with local families at weekends. Depending on the season it colours with flowers, and its paths and viewpoints look out over the same coastline that produces the famous dunes — a calm, uncrowded green break rather than a headline attraction.

item.title: Uminonakamichi Seaside Park — Guide
item.description: Uminonakamichi Seaside Park is an enormous national government park spread across the scenic Uminonakamichi sandbar that stretches into Hakata Bay, offering a full day of nature and family fun. Its highlight is the seasonal flower gardens, which blaze with colour through the year — nemophila and tulips in spring, sunflowers and roses in summer, cosmos and kochia in autumn — creating spectacular flower carpets and photo spots. Alongside the flowers, the vast grounds hold a small animal park and petting zoo, a summer water park with pools and slides, wide lawns, cycling paths with rental bikes, and sea views.

item.title: Boso Flower Fields Guide: Minamiboso Blooms & Access
item.description: Thanks to its mild, frost-free maritime climate, the southern tip of the Boso Peninsula bursts into flower while much of Japan is still cold — making Minamiboso and Tateyama a beloved late-winter and spring flower destination. Along the scenic Boso Flower Line coastal road, fields glow with poppies, rapeseed, stocks and marigolds, and “flower-picking gardens” let visitors pick their own blooms to take home from as early as January. Set between blue Pacific coastline and the green slopes near Mount Nokogiri, the flower fields make a colourful, family-friendly day out and one of the prettiest spring drives near Tokyo.

item.title: Furano Lavender Guide: Best Time, Farms & Festival (Jul)
item.description: For a few glorious weeks each July, the hills around Furano turn purple as Hokkaido’s famous lavender fields come into bloom — one of Japan’s great summer sights. Rows of fragrant lavender sweep toward the mountains, joined by rainbow ribbons of poppies, salvia and marigolds, all under crisp northern skies. The legendary Farm Tomita leads a cluster of flower farms offering viewing, lavender soft cream and sweets, picking experiences and festivals.

item.title: Saitama Nature: Shibazakura, Chichibu Mountains & Nagatoro Gorge
item.description: Saitama Prefecture stretches from the flat agricultural plains immediately north of Tokyo all the way into the Chichibu mountain range along its western edge. This geographic range — from gentle river valleys and lotus wetlands in the east to dense cedar forests and alpine ridgelines in the west — gives the prefecture a seasonal variety that surprises most visitors who think of it primarily as suburban Tokyo. The Arakawa River cuts through dramatic rock gorges.
